decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Fuel subsidies were enormous and fiscally wasteful, and the report says richer households benefited most.
Inflation surged and poverty worsened in late 2022.
The IMF said higher oil prices were not turned into fiscal space or reserves.
The CBN tightening cycle shows the severity of the macro problem rather than a clean policy success.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Lower-middle-income, large-population economy with oil dependence, subsidy distortion, exchange-rate stress, and limited fiscal room.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Partial: Buhari had fiscal authority and appointment power, but oil theft, prices, and global shocks heavily shaped outcomes.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Subsidy policy remained a major drag on public finances.
The household welfare picture deteriorated.
The IMF says the oil-price opportunity was not captured.

evaluations.source_mix: World Bank, IMF, Central Bank of Nigeria, and official government releases; strong on policy and macro distress, weaker on independent project-level outcome audits.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: Nigeria is a lower-middle-income country with GDP per capita about 2899.2, GNI per capita about 4754.8, and population about 223.2 million.
evaluations.chapter_rationale: Buhari scores 3.0/10 because the year is dominated by subsidy distortion, inflation, and poverty pressure, even though there were some genuine reform moves and technocratic appointments. The positive items are real but too small relative to the scale of macro mismanagement and the inability to turn high oil prices into stronger fiscal space or household welfare. This is below the middle band because the year's macro record is clearly weak, but not quite at the floor because the administration did still pass reforms and maintain some institutional functionality.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would require clearer evidence of total state failure or direct economic predation. The file shows serious weakness, but not complete collapse.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would need evidence that reforms materially reduced subsidy waste and stabilized inflation or poverty. The record points strongly the other way.

chapter_specific.value: Subsidy burdens, oil theft, inflation, and exchange-rate strain dominated.
Some social and health reforms existed, but households faced rising poverty and prices.
Clearly weak stewardship overall, with reform gestures insufficient to offset macro deterioration.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Targeted relief under the PM package shows an immediate household response to crisis.
The budget aimed to raise taxes on the rich and target a fiscal deficit under IMF pressure.
Budget speech austerity and tax-leakage efforts show a real attempt at stabilization.
The IMF agreement points to a sizable fiscal and exchange-rate adjustment package.
The IMF review says the authorities had taken important corrective measures.
The central-bank governor appointment adds some technocratic capacity to the response.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The economy was already in a balance-of-payments crisis with very low reserves and high inflation.
Inflation remained severe late in 2022, showing the stabilization was incomplete.
The IMF still linked weakness to earlier policy choices and external stress.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Lower-middle-income economy under IMF pressure, with reserve exhaustion, inflation, and a politically constrained coalition government.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Partial: Sharif's cabinet made real policy adjustments, but the macro picture was heavily inherited and externally constrained.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The macro crisis was severe when he took office.
Inflation remained high by year-end.
The IMF review shows the situation was only partially fixed.

evaluations.source_mix: Primarily Pakistani finance ministry, IMF, Reuters, and local reporting; strong on policy response, weaker on independent outcome verification.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: Pakistan is a lower-middle-income economy with GDP per capita about 1538.3, GNI per capita about 5374.3, and population about 243.7 million.
evaluations.chapter_rationale: Sharif scores 4.0/10 because the cabinet did mount a serious stabilization response, but it did so in the context of a severe inherited crisis and without enough time or evidence to show broad prosperity gains. The record includes targeted relief, fiscal tightening, IMF-backed reform, and some technocratic staffing, yet inflation and the external-balance emergency remained severe. That places the year in the mixed-to-weak band: better than passivity, but not good enough to count as a genuine prosperity turnaround.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would understate the seriousness of the government’s corrective package and the fact that some stabilization work was actually undertaken. The record is not empty.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require proof that the stabilization package had already restored broad household welfare or macro stability. The evidence shows only partial correction by year-end.

chapter_specific.value: IMF dependence, external-balance stress, and inflation dominated the year.
Targeted relief helped on paper, but the crisis environment remained severe for households.
A partial stabilization government, not a prosperity breakthrough.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Marcos named an experienced economic team and made the economy the first priority.
The planning chief appointment was presented as technocratic rather than partisan.
The SONA laid out fiscal and tax reforms, investment, and customs measures.
Tariff reductions on food and energy imports were a concrete anti-price measure.
The debt-to-GDP ratio fell below target at end-2022.
Agricultural support and food-security interventions were actually being implemented.
Kadiwa coverage reached more than a million households and many farmer groups.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Inflation remained high, reducing real household gains.
Employment recovery was incomplete and uneven by region.
Debt was lower than target but still high, so fiscal improvement was partial.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Lower-middle-income recovery economy with inflation, post-pandemic normalization, and large household price pressure.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Moderate to high for appointments and policy direction, but many outcomes also reflect reopening and inherited post-pandemic conditions.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Inflation remained a major drag on welfare.
Labor-market recovery was real but uneven.
Debt improvement was real but not yet transformative.

evaluations.source_mix: Reuters, PSA, DOF, PCO, PNA, and legal texts; the file mixes direct presidential policy with official outcome statistics.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The Philippines is a lower-middle-income economy with GDP per capita about 3548.1, GNI per capita about 9058.8, and population about 114.0 million.
evaluations.chapter_rationale: Marcos scores 6.0/10 because 2022 shows a credible first-year policy package, technocratic staffing, and some real household and fiscal support, alongside moderate macro improvement. Inflation remained painful and the labor-market recovery was incomplete, so the score cannot move into the high band, but the evidence is better than a merely mixed transition year because policy choices were concrete and some outcomes were positive. In short, this is a reasonably competent early stewardship record with visible but not yet decisive distributional gains.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would discount the technocratic appointments, debt improvement, and concrete food/energy interventions. The year was not just a speech year.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require stronger proof that inflation was tamed and household gains were broad and durable. The record does not yet show that.

chapter_specific.value: Inflation and post-pandemic normalization defined the year.
Food support and labor recovery helped households, but inflation still eroded purchasing power.
Better than inherited and broadly competent, though still mostly a first-year transition score.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The central bank raised rates to fight inflation, showing some stabilization capacity remained.
The IMF said emergency financial and monetary measures temporarily stabilized the financial sector.
Reappointing Nabiullina signaled a desire to preserve macro stabilization capacity.
Putin ordered new budget rules, a direct fiscal response to sanctions and downturn.
Targeted benefits for displaced people were a real but narrow welfare response.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: OECD said sanctions, capital isolation, and a severe downturn hit Russia hard.
Freedom House describes a centralized and corrupt patronage system.
Asset immobilization and sanctions froze huge amounts of Russian state wealth.
Reuters data show collapsing consumer demand and falling real incomes.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: War economy under massive sanctions, asset freezes, international isolation, and a highly personalist political system.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: High at the system level because the invasion and wartime governance choices are Putin's, even where the central bank remains operationally independent.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The invasion-triggered sanctions regime devastated the macro environment.
Household demand and incomes fell sharply.
The patronage/corruption system is directly harmful to fair prosperity.

evaluations.source_mix: IMF, OECD, Freedom House, Reuters, Treasury, and World Bank sanctions context; strong evidence of harm and limited stabilization.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: Russia is an upper-middle-income war economy with GDP per capita about 15619.6, GNI per capita about 26991.8, and population about 144.2 million.
evaluations.chapter_rationale: Putin scores 2.0/10 because 2022 is defined by war, sanctions, asset freezes, and a major contraction in household welfare, with only limited stabilization responses softening the blow. The positive items are narrow and mainly defensive: central-bank tightening, budget-rule changes, and targeted benefits, none of which offset the broad economic damage from the invasion and the coercive political system. This is near the floor because the evidence shows severe, ruler-linked destruction of prosperity rather than ordinary crisis management.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would require even clearer realized economic catastrophe or total administrative breakdown. The record is already extremely negative, but there is still some stabilization capacity and targeted relief.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require evidence that the regime preserved broad prosperity or that the war shock was largely outside Putin's control. The evidence makes the opposite case.

chapter_specific.value: War, sanctions, asset freezes, and international isolation overwhelmingly shaped 2022.
Targeted transfers softened damage, but consumer demand and real incomes still fell.
Severely negative overall, with limited stabilization unable to offset war-economy destruction.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The World Bank said Thailand recovered to pre-pandemic output and the government kept proactive fiscal support.
Parliament passed a large budget aimed at recovery and aid distribution.
Tourism support and domestic-travel subsidies were concrete recovery tools.
EV incentives and investment-barrier removal show a real attempt to attract future investment.
Fiscal policy was being redirected toward vulnerable groups as the recovery progressed.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Rural poverty and inequality remained structurally high.
Household debt and fragile recovery limited the strength of the rebound.
Investment applications were expected to fall, showing an incomplete recovery.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Upper-middle-income economy with tourism dependence, household debt, rural poverty, and reopening effects after the pandemic.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Mixed: Prayut-era fiscal and cabinet choices matter, but reopening and tourism normalization were also large drivers.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Rural poverty and inequality remain high.
Household debt and a fragile recovery are major negatives.
Investment weakness limits the trajectory.

evaluations.source_mix: World Bank, IMF, BOT, Reuters, and official Thai budget/tourism material; mostly primary or near-primary sources.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: Thailand is an upper-middle-income economy with GDP per capita about 6909.4, GNI per capita about 16886.5, and population about 71.7 million.
evaluations.chapter_rationale: Prayut scores 5.5/10 because 2022 saw a real post-pandemic recovery, active fiscal support, and policy moves on tourism and investment, but those positives sit alongside persistent rural poverty, household debt, and weak investment momentum. This is better than a simply mixed score because the government did produce concrete recovery tools, yet it is not higher because the recovery was still shallow and the structural distribution problems remained large. The result is a modestly positive stewardship judgment rather than a robust prosperity verdict.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the clear recovery, budget support, and investment-promotion measures in the file. The government did more than coast.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require stronger evidence of durable distributional improvement and a less fragile investment outlook. The structural poverty and debt evidence keeps it below that range.

chapter_specific.value: Tourism reopening, household debt, and fragile rural incomes dominated.
Targeted support helped, but inequality and debt remained high.
Moderate recovery with meaningful support, but not enough structural change for a higher score.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Energy and food support for vulnerable groups was a concrete mitigation step.
Growth and tourism recovered in the first half of 2022, so the economy was not uniformly collapsing.
Employment had recovered and minimum-wage hikes provided some near-term relief.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Inflation reached extreme levels and producer prices were even worse.
The IMF described the low-rate, intervention-heavy model as distortionary and risky.
Erdogan's own public push for still-lower rates shows direct commitment to the policy mix behind the crisis.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Upper-middle-income economy with a currency crisis, energy shock exposure, and a policy regime that favored ultra-low interest rates.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: High: the low-rate model and appointed team were core Erdoğan choices, though some growth was helped by tourism and exports.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The inflation shock was extreme and damaging to households.
Independent surveillance says the policy model itself was distortionary.
Erdoğan publicly doubled down on the low-rate approach.

evaluations.source_mix: World Bank, OECD, IMF, and Reuters; a strong macro dossier where the attribution to Erdogan is unusually direct.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: Turkey is an upper-middle-income economy with GDP per capita about 10897.8, GNI per capita about 32833.5, and population about 85.0 million.
evaluations.chapter_rationale: Erdoğan scores 2.5/10 because 2022 is dominated by the consequences of his low-rate monetary doctrine: runaway inflation, currency stress, and falling real incomes. There are mitigating positives such as wage hikes, relief payments, and some output growth, but these do not offset the scale of the macro damage and the explicit evidence that the policy mix was distortionary. This sits near the low end of the scale because the ruler's own choices are tightly linked to the harm and because the relief measures were too small to change the overall picture.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would imply a more complete collapse than the record shows. There was still growth, tourism recovery, and household support, even if they were overwhelmed by inflation.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would need evidence that the low-rate strategy produced durable prosperity or that inflation was successfully contained. The file shows the opposite: very high inflation and eroding real incomes.

chapter_specific.value: Currency crisis, energy shocks, and a low-rate policy regime defined the year.
Assistance and wage hikes helped some households, but inflation crushed purchasing power.
One of the weakest stewardship records in the batch.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The deficit fell sharply in FY2022, indicating fiscal normalization as emergency spending rolled off.
Commerce began concrete semiconductor-industry support design.
CHIPS implementation leadership was established for a major industrial-policy rollout.
Brookings described the infrastructure package as a major jobs and growth opportunity.
The Treasury framed the Inflation Reduction Act as lowering costs, boosting jobs, and reducing the deficit.
Biden explicitly affirmed Fed independence in the inflation fight.
Jobs remained strong, with payroll growth and wages still rising.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The Census Bureau shows poverty and especially child poverty rose in 2022 under inflation pressure.
Much of the positive legislation was still prospective rather than fully realized in 2022.
Workforce shortages and implementation limits could blunt gains from the industrial policy agenda.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: High-income economy with inflation, Fed tightening, and post-pandemic adjustment affecting household welfare and budget outcomes.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Moderate: Biden had clear influence over industrial policy and public budgeting, but inflation, labor markets, and the Fed were also shaped by independent and global forces.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Poverty and child poverty rose despite strong macro indicators.
Implementation and workforce constraints remain real.
Several major policy effects were still prospective.

evaluations.source_mix: Treasury, Commerce, Census, Reuters, Brookings, Tax Policy Center, and PWBM; strong mix of official data and independent policy analysis.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The United States is a high-income economy with GDP per capita about 76657.2, GNI per capita about 65564.9, and population about 334.0 million.
evaluations.chapter_rationale: Biden scores 6.5/10 because 2022 combined strong labor markets, major industrial-policy enactments, and clear fiscal normalization with a real inflation-hit to household welfare. The positive side is substantial: semiconductor policy, infrastructure and IRA implementation, deficit reduction, and explicit respect for Fed independence. The negative side is also real: poverty and especially child poverty rose, and much of the industrial-policy promise was still ahead of the 2022 outcome window. That places the year in the good-but-not-exceptional range rather than the high band.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the strength of the labor market, fiscal normalization, and major policy architecture laid in 2022. The year was more than just inflation pain.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require stronger realized household gains and less reliance on prospective policy effects. The poverty data and implementation caveats keep it below that level.

chapter_specific.value: Inflation, Fed tightening, and post-pandemic adjustment shaped the year.
Jobs were strong and some legislation was progressive, but poverty rose under inflation pressure.
Competent macro and industrial policy, but household outcomes were mixed rather than transformative.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The IMF says Vietnam had robust growth and sound fundamentals with prudent policies and strong external buffers.
The IMF projected continued growth with inflation below target.
The World Bank projected a strong rebound and high growth for 2022.
Year-end inflation met the National Assembly target.
Realized state investment and FDI were both substantial.
FDI inflows were strong by year-end.
The plenum report shows direct party leadership over 2022 performance and 2023 planning.
Trọng himself described most targets as achieved or surpassed in the year-end interview.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Reuters reported that the anti-graft drive was chilling supply chains and investment.
The anti-corruption campaign had material market costs and investor confidence effects.
The World Bank pointed to serious skills and tertiary-education gaps.
Household vulnerability and poverty reduction setbacks persisted after COVID.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Lower-middle-income fast-growth economy with strong export integration, but also skills gaps and some anti-corruption side effects.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Moderate to high at the party-state level, but many outcomes are system-level and not a direct personal action transcript.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The anti-graft campaign imposed real transaction costs.
Skills and education gaps remained a drag on higher productivity.
Vulnerability and inequality were not fully solved.

evaluations.source_mix: IMF, World Bank, official Vietnamese statistics and party-state reporting, plus Reuters analysis; a strong outcome-and-policy mix with some promotional bias in official material.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: Vietnam is a lower-middle-income fast-growth economy with GDP per capita about 4147.7, GNI per capita about 10814.0, and population about 99.7 million.
evaluations.chapter_rationale: Trọng scores 7.0/10 because 2022 combines strong growth, low inflation, significant FDI and public investment, and a continued policy emphasis on macro stability. The main negatives are not macro collapse but the side effects of the anti-corruption drive and persistent skills or productivity gaps that limit how broad and durable the gains can be. This is one of the stronger prosperity scores in the batch because the economy clearly moved forward, but it remains below the very top because implementation quality, distributional detail, and the anti-graft side effects are still imperfectly verified.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the robust growth, controlled inflation, and strong FDI evidence. Vietnam's 2022 record is not merely rhetorical or stagnant.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require cleaner proof that growth translated into more even household gains and that anti-corruption did not materially impede normal economic activity. The file shows both accomplishments and meaningful friction.

chapter_specific.value: Reopening, global demand, and supply-chain shifts aided the year.
Broad growth and low inflation helped, but education and procurement constraints remained.
Among the stronger stewardship cases, though anti-corruption side effects and attribution limits keep it below exceptional.

batch_notes: Calibration anchors used a low/high split: Russia and Turkey/Iran/Nigeria as low anchors, Germany/Indonesia/USA/Vietnam as high anchors, with Brazil/Mexico/Pakistan/Philippines as middle references.
Scores were set from ruler-attributed choices plus implementation or outcome evidence; announcements without follow-through were discounted rather than mechanically scored upward.
Coverage statuses were treated as advisory bookkeeping only; no available dossier was marked unavailable.
Missing or weak lenses widened confidence ranges and lowered certainty, but they did not mechanically cap scores or force nulls.
